subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw support a cross-machine Chrome extension browser relay again, and if so should it be restored directly or require a browser-backend/plugin API first?
rationale: The missing workflow is a real shipped regression for affected users, but the fix defines remote browser-control authority over signed-in sessions and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Design secure plugin/API replacement
options.body: Land or sponsor a browser-backend/plugin API and implement the relay as an optional package with explicit auth, tab scope, audit logs, migration, and security review.

options.title: Restore legacy relay directly
options.body: Reintroduce the old driver path in core, accepting a larger security and compatibility burden to restore the managed-hosting workflow faster.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Document that cross-machine browser control must use node hosts or remote CDP and close the restoration path as not planned.

recommendation.title: Design secure plugin/API replacement
recommendation.body: Land or sponsor a browser-backend/plugin API and implement the relay as an optional package with explicit auth, tab scope, audit logs, migration, and security review.

likelyOwner.reason: This account authored and merged the removal/migration PR and has the clearest history on the current browser MCP replacement boundary.
